generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from a pool of realistic short strings; 5% of rows get a near-variant of a pool value (case flip, trailing space, one-char edit); 2% get '' when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_id: Sample from a pool of realistic identifier strings (lowercase letters + digits, 8-10 chars); 5% near-variants (case flip, one-char edit); 2% '' when nullable; boundary literals from per_column_exceptions are injected into the pool verbatim.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Sample from a pool of realistic person/place names; 5% near-variants (case flip, trailing space); 2% '' when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_note: Sample from a small pool of note strings; 90% NULL when nullable, else a pool value.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_small: Uniform integer in [0, 20]; 5% at min-1/max+1 boundary when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_year: Uniform integer in [1909, 2011]; 5% at min-1/max+1 boundary.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_count: Uniform integer in [0, 100]; 5% at min-1/max+1 boundary.
generic_sampling_rules.text_numeric: Numeric value rendered as TEXT, uniform integer in [0, 400]; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_flag: One of a small enum pool; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, 5-30% of generated rows are NULL (per column statistics), at least one NULL row per nullable column; NOT NULL and primary-key columns never get NULL; FK-parent join-key columns listed in UNMATCHED_PARENT get at most 20% NULL so unused non-NULL parent values remain for unmatched-parent targets; other nullable FK child columns use the general 5-30% share.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates: For DISTINCT-target columns, 20-50% of rows share a value with another row; planting runs only on non-PK columns or after PK re-dedup; post-generation verify the share on surviving rows.
generic_sampling_rules.ties: For ORDER/LIMIT-target columns, plant at least two rows tied at the listed rank; when the tie target is an aggregate (SUM/COUNT/COALESCE), construct the underlying per-group values so the aggregate ties at the specified rank with no smaller value present, and plant after PK/UNIQUE dedup and NULL application; re-verify after final re-dedup and after write-time skips.
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_parent: For each UNMATCHED_PARENT target, reserve at least one non-NULL parent value (or full parent tuple for composite keys) never drawn by any child; verify after generation and after write-time skips that at least one parent row with a non-NULL key has no child.
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: For GROUP_SIZE targets, plant groups of size 1, 2 and >=3 on non-key columns or on rows whose PK components are not disturbed; re-verify after final re-dedup and after write-time skips.
generic_sampling_rules.hard_bounds: All range, enum and order rules in semantic_rules_and_formulas are hard constraints: every generated row must satisfy them on non-NULL operands; clamp numeric output to [lo,hi] after any jitter.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 14/20 units fail with ValueError('empty range for randrange() (504, 101, -403)'). This originates in NumberSampler.sample(): when lo/hi are set (e.g. lo=1, hi=2 for 'half', lo=1, hi=3 for 'stint', lo=1, hi=10 for 'rank'), the code still applies the boundary jitter `v += d` / `v -= 2*d` and then `_cast`, but more importantly the `_fresh_or_reuse` path uses `r.randint(int(lo), int(hi))`; the failure range (504, 101) indicates `list_min`/`list_max` were computed from original values (e.g. 504) while `self.max` was overridden to 101 (COUNT_MAX) or similar, producing an inverted range. Specifically `self.list_max = min(self.max, _MAX)` but `self.list_min = min(self.elements)` is NOT clamped to `self.max`, so when original values exceed the spec hi (e.g. a count column with original value 504 and spec hi=100), `randint(list_min, list_max)` = randint(504, 100) raises. This blocks generation for the majority of instances.
issues.requested_revision: In NumberSampler.__init__, clamp list_min/list_max to [self.min, self.max] after applying lo/hi overrides (e.g. self.list_min = max(self.min, min(self.list_min, self.max)); self.list_max = max(self.list_min, min(self.list_max, self.max))). Also guard the jitter so the final value stays within [self.min, self.max] for spec-bounded columns. Re-run generation and confirm n_fail == 0.

issues.evidence: Validity feedback: all 6 produced instances report 'no_rows_added' and 'compact_rows_missing'. writer.write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one as `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)` with orig_path defaulting to None, so the compact database is never copied (shutil.copyfile is skipped) and the .part file is created empty. The docstring and module comment claim 'the instance file is a copy of the compact database with the generated rows appended', but the CLI never passes orig_path. This violates the stated Round-1 adaptation and the preservation-of-compact-rows requirement.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. add orig_path to the args dict in cli.main and call write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, orig_path=a['orig'])), so each unit is a copy of the compact DB with generated rows appended. Verify compact_rows_missing == 0 and no_rows_added == 0 in the validity report.

issues.evidence: spec.NULL_TARGETS includes ('Master','playerID'), ('Master','coachID'), ('Teams','tmID'), ('HOF','hofID'), ('Coaches','coachID'), ('Scoring','playerID'), ('Goalies','SHO'). Several of these are primary-key or NOT NULL columns: Master.playerID is not declared NOT NULL in the schema but is the FK target of many tables; Teams.tmID is part of the PK (year,tmID) and NOT NULL; HOF.hofID is NOT NULL primary key; Coaches.coachID is part of PK and NOT NULL. _apply_null_rule correctly skips cm.notnull or cm.pk_pos>0, so these NULL targets are silently never satisfied. The spec's null_targets list therefore contradicts the schema's NOT NULL/PK constraints and the interface rule 'NOT NULL / primary-key columns never get NULL'. The spec should not list PK/NOT NULL columns as NULL targets.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: remove Teams.tmID, HOF.hofID, Coaches.coachID (and any other PK/NOT NULL column) from spec NULL_TARGETS, or explicitly document that they are exempt. Engineer: ensure the NULL rule is applied only to genuinely nullable columns and that the spec's null_targets list is consistent with the schema.

issues.evidence: instance._plant_ties only plants two rows sharing a value in the target column, but the spec's tie targets are on aggregates: Goalies.playerID tie_on SUM(goalies.sho) DESC, Master.birthCountry tie_on COUNT(*) ASC and DESC, Goalies.SHO tie_on COALESCE(goalies.sho,0). Planting two equal SHO values does not guarantee a tie at rank 1 of SUM(sho) per playerID, nor a tie at rank 1/8 of COUNT(*) per birthCountry. Similarly _plant_group_sizes picks three values and assigns counts 1,2,3 but does not ensure the resulting groups survive the subsequent PK/UNIQUE dedup and NULL rule (which may overwrite the planted values). The construction_pairs feedback shows only 29/288 separated, consistent with these targets not being reliably realized.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: implement tie/group-size planting after PK/UNIQUE dedup and NULL application, and for aggregate tie targets (SUM, COUNT) construct the underlying per-group values so the aggregate ties at the specified rank. Designer: clarify in the spec that tie targets are on the aggregate expression, not the raw column, and that group-size targets must survive dedup.

issues.evidence: The spec's semantic_rules_and_formulas include many CHECK-like constraints (e.g. Teams.G > 0, Teams.rank BETWEEN 1 AND 10, Master.height 60-90, Master.weight 100-300, HOF.year 1945-2011, AwardsPlayers.year 1917-2011, Coaches.stint 1-3, Scoring.stint 1-4, GoaliesShootout.stint 1-2, ScoringShootout.stint 1-3, CombinedShutouts.month 1-12, date 1-31, R/P IN ('R','P'), abbrev.Type enum, etc.). The program's NumberSampler applies jitter (`v += d`, `v -= 2*d`) after drawing within [lo,hi], which can push values outside the spec range (e.g. rank=10 -> 11, month=12 -> 13, height=90 -> 91). The spec does not state that these are hard constraints that must hold on every generated row, nor does the program clamp after jitter. This is an inconsistency between the stated formulas and the sampler behavior.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: state explicitly whether the semantic formulas are hard constraints (must hold on all generated rows) or soft/statistical. Engineer: if hard, clamp NumberSampler output to [lo,hi] after jitter for spec-bounded columns, and add a post-generation validation pass that checks each formula on non-NULL operands and reports violations.

issues.evidence: instance._plant_unmatched_parent is a no-op (returns cols unchanged) with a comment claiming the property is 'naturally satisfied'. However, fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws child FK values with replacement from the parent's generated values, and for small child tables (e.g. AwardsCoaches 20 rows, HOF 30 rows) it is possible that every parent value is used, leaving no parent row without children. The spec's unmatched_join_rows targets (parent_rows_without_children: true) are therefore not guaranteed. The construction_pairs feedback (29/288 separated) is consistent with this not being reliably realized.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: implement _plant_unmatched_parent to explicitly reserve at least one parent value that is never drawn by any child (e.g. after building children, if all parent values are used, replace one child FK with a different parent value or add a sentinel parent row). Verify with a post-generation check that each UNMATCHED_PARENT target has at least one parent row with no child.

issues.evidence: Reproducibility feedback: 'reproducible': false. cli._one seeds rng with `random.Random(a['seed_base'] * 100003 + i)`, which is deterministic per unit, but the multiprocessing path and the `p = 0.0 if rng.random() < 0.3 else 0.2` in build_random_instance, plus the use of `rng.sample`/`rng.shuffle` in planting functions, should be deterministic. The non-reproducibility likely stems from the fact that the 14 failing units raise before writing, and the 6 succeeding units may differ across runs if the failure point depends on dict iteration order (schema.tables is a dict; iteration order is insertion order from sqlite_master, which is stable, but `sorted({...})` in _make_spec_sampler and `rng.sample(vals, 3)` depend on the order of `vals` which comes from `cols[c]` — stable). The more likely cause is that the run was executed twice with different random state due to the `p` draw consuming rng before the failure, and the failure itself is non-deterministic because `randint(504, 101)` depends on which column is sampled first, which depends on dict order. Regardless, the feedback explicitly reports non-reproducible, which must be fixed.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: after fixing the randrange bug, re-run generation twice with the same seed and confirm identical instance files (byte-for-byte or via a hash). Ensure all randomness flows through the per-unit rng and that no global random state or set/dict iteration order affects output.

Whether the spec's table_sizes_per_instance (e.g. Master 200, Scoring 200) are achievable given the PK/UNIQUE dedup and NULL rule — the jitter in choose_table_sizes (0.5x-1.5x) may reduce effective sizes below the spec, and dedup may further reduce them.
Whether the 'no_rows_added' validity reason is solely due to the missing orig_path copy or also due to all generated rows being rejected by PK/UNIQUE constraints — needs re-run after the writer fix.

issues.evidence: spec.py NULL_TARGETS lists ('Master','playerID') and ('Scoring','playerID'), and instance.py _apply_null_rule plants NULLs into every nullable column including these. But Master.playerID is the parent of many FK children (AwardsPlayers, Goalies, Scoring, CombinedShutouts, ...) and Scoring.playerID is a child FK to Master. The execution feedback shows Master.playerID NULL 469/3876 and Scoring.playerID NULL 639/3609. The schema declares Master.playerID as a plain TEXT column (nullable), so NULLs are legal, but the spec's own 'unmatched_join_rows' target for Master.playerID requires 'child_rows_with_null_fk: true' AND 'parent_rows_without_children: true' — the program satisfies the first by accident (NULL FKs) but the second is only checked via _reserve_unmatched_parents, which skips NULL parent values. More importantly, the spec's per-column exception for Master.playerID 'null_rows' with 'null_share 5-30%' is being applied to a column that is the join key for nearly every table; the resulting NULL parent rows make the 'parent_rows_without_children' target trivially true for the wrong reason (NULL parent, not an unused value). This is a specification/implementation mismatch: the spec should either exclude Master.playerID from NULL_TARGETS (it is the primary join key) or the program must ensure the unmatched-parent reservation is on non-NULL parent values, which _reserve_unmatched_parents does but only after NULLs are planted, so the 'unused' set is computed over non-NULL parents — acceptable — yet the NULL parent rows still inflate the 'parent_rows_without_children' count. Request: clarify in spec whether Master.playerID NULLs are intended; if yes, document that unmatched-parent is satisfied by non-NULL unused values only; if no, remove from NULL_TARGETS.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: state explicitly whether Master.playerID (and Scoring.playerID) may be NULL, and whether the unmatched-parent target must be satisfied by a non-NULL unused parent value. Engineer: if NULLs are disallowed for these join keys, drop them from NULL_TARGETS and from the generic nullable-column NULL planting for FK-parent columns.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_ties for the 'SUM(SHO)' target sets cols['SHO'][idx[0]] = '5' and cols['SHO'][idx[1]] = '5' on two rows of Goalies, but Goalies.SHO is a TEXT column and the tie is on SUM(goalies.sho). SQLite SUM over TEXT '5' coerces to 5, so the tie works numerically, but the spec's Goalies.SHO tie target is 'COALESCE(goalies.sho, 0)' ASC and DESC — the program plants '5' for both the SUM and COALESCE branches, which does not guarantee a tie at rank 1 for the COALESCE target when other rows also have SHO='5' or when NULLs are present (COALESCE(NULL,0)=0). The execution feedback shows Goalies.SHO NULL 77/1727, so COALESCE ties at 0 are likely, but the planted '5' rows do not ensure the rank-1 tie for the COALESCE target. Also _plant_ties runs before _apply_null_rule? No — it runs after, per the code order in build_random_instance (NULL rule, then dedup, then _plant_group_sizes, _plant_ties, _plant_duplicates). So the planted '5' survives, but the COALESCE tie is not specifically constructed.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: for the COALESCE(SHO,0) tie target, plant two rows with the same non-NULL SHO value AND ensure no other row has a strictly smaller COALESCE value (or plant two NULL rows so COALESCE=0 ties at the minimum). For the SUM(SHO) target, ensure the two chosen players have no other Goalies rows that would change their SUM, or set the SUM explicitly by controlling all rows of those players.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_group_sizes for ('Master','playerID') and ('Goalies','playerID') overwrites values in the PK column after sample_fresh_primary_keys has deduplicated. For Master.playerID this is not a PK (Master has no declared PK in the schema — playerID is nullable TEXT), so overwriting is safe for uniqueness, but for Goalies.playerID the PK is (playerID, year, stint); overwriting playerID after dedup can create duplicate (playerID, year, stint) tuples if the overwritten value collides with an existing row's (playerID, year, stint). The execution feedback reports pk_duplicates: 0, so in practice the collision did not occur in the 20 instances, but the code does not re-dedup after _plant_group_sizes. Same risk for _plant_duplicates on Master.playerID (not a PK, safe) and Master.coachID (not a PK, safe).
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: re-run sample_fresh_primary_keys after _plant_group_sizes and _plant_duplicates, or restrict group-size/duplicate planting to non-PK columns. Add an assertion that PK uniqueness holds after planting.

issues.evidence: spec.py BOUNDARY for ('Master','height') is ['71','72','73','74','75','76'] and the semantic rule is CAST(REPLACE(height,'/','') AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 60 AND 90. The program's NumberSampler for height uses lo=60, hi=90 and clamps, so boundary values 71-76 are within range, but the spec's comparison_boundary target also lists expression_values [71,72,73] for the REPLACE expression. The program does not plant the '/' form (e.g. '6/1' for 61) that the REPLACE expression implies; it only plants plain integers. The execution feedback does not show height values, but the spec's expression_values target is not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: clarify whether height values may contain '/' (the REPLACE suggests they do in the original data). Engineer: if so, plant at least one height value with a '/' that evaluates to a boundary value (e.g. '7/1' -> 71) so the REPLACE expression boundary is exercised.

issues.evidence: instance.py _reserve_unmatched_parents iterates spec.UNMATCHED_PARENT which includes ('Teams','year') and ('Teams','tmID'). Teams.year is part of the PK (year, tmID) and is NOT NULL, so it cannot be NULL; the reservation rewrites child FKs to free one parent value. But for ('Teams','year') the child FKs are composite (year, tmID) pairs; the code treats year and tmID independently, so freeing a year value does not guarantee a Teams row with that year has no child — a child may still reference (year, other_tmID). The execution feedback does not report unmatched-parent verification results, so this is unverified.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: for composite-FK unmatched-parent targets, reserve a full parent tuple (year, tmID) that no child references, and verify post-generation that at least one Teams row has no child in Coaches/Scoring/Goalies/etc. Add a post-generation assertion.

issues.evidence: The spec's semantic_rules_and_formulas include 'Master.deathYear >= birthYear' as a conditional rule, but the program's NumberSampler for deathYear and birthYear draws independently from [1909,2011] with no cross-column constraint. The execution feedback does not report a violation count for this rule, and the spec's uncertainty section acknowledges it is 'not enforced by schema'. The program does not implement it, so generated rows may violate it.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: either drop the deathYear >= birthYear rule (it is not a schema constraint and the spec marks it uncertain) or promote it to a hard rule. Engineer: if kept, enforce it in build_random_instance by resampling deathYear >= birthYear when both are non-NULL.

issues.evidence: values.py NumberSampler.sample applies jitter (v += d, v -= d, etc.) and then _clamp to [min,max]. For columns with lo=hi (e.g. half with lo=1, hi=2 is fine, but stint for GoaliesShootout is lo=1, hi=2, and for Scoring lo=1, hi=4), the jitter is clamped, so the value stays in range — good. However, for the 'rank' column with lo=1, hi=10, the jitter can push a value to 0 or 11 before clamping, and clamping restores it to 1 or 10, which is correct. No issue here; noted as verified.

issues.evidence: spec.py NULL_TARGETS includes ('Goalies','SHO') and instance._apply_null_rule plants NULLs for it, but the execution feedback shows 'Goalies.SHO: generated rows: NULL 126 / 1671' — that is fine. However, the spec's per_column_exceptions for Goalies.SHO ties_for_order_limit requires a COALESCE(SHO,0) tie at rank 1 with 'no row has a smaller non-NULL value'. instance._plant_ties 'coalesce' branch only rewrites values < 0 to '0' (SHO is generated in [0,100] so this never fires) and plants two NULLs. But the tie is planted BEFORE the final sample_fresh_primary_keys/drop_unique_duplicates re-dedup, and more importantly the two NULL rows are chosen by rng.shuffle over indices of the Goalies table — if those two rows are later dropped by PK re-dedup (Goalies PK is (playerID,year,stint)), the planted NULLs may not survive. There is no post-planting assertion that the COALESCE tie actually exists. Same fragility applies to the SUM(SHO) tie: _plant_ties sets SHO='5' on two rows and caps others at 5, but the final re-dedup can drop one of the two tied rows, and the 'cap every other SHO so no other player's SUM exceeds 5' logic caps per-row SHO, not per-player SUM — a player with multiple Goalies rows each SHO=5 will have SUM=10 > 5, breaking the 'no smaller value present' requirement for the rank-1 tie.
issues.requested_revision: After the final PK/UNIQUE re-dedup in build_random_instance, re-verify (and if needed re-plant) the aggregate tie targets: for SUM(SHO) ensure exactly the two chosen players have the maximal per-player SUM and that no other player's SUM equals or exceeds it (cap per-player SUM, not per-row SHO); for COALESCE(SHO,0) ensure at least two surviving rows have NULL SHO and no surviving row has a non-NULL SHO < 0. Add an assertion or a post-planting repair pass so the tie survives dedup.

issues.evidence: spec.py UNMATCHED_PARENT includes ('Teams','year') and ('Teams','tmID') with the note 'unmatched_satisfied_by: full unused (year,tmID) tuple'. instance._reserve_unmatched_parents iterates over UNMATCHED_PARENT entries independently and, for each (pt,pc), collects child FK columns referencing that single column and frees one parent value if all are used. For composite-key targets (Teams.year, Teams.tmID) this treats each column separately, not the full (year,tmID) tuple. A child row (e.g. Coaches) matches a Teams parent only when BOTH year and tmID match; freeing a single year value or a single tmID value does not guarantee an unused (year,tmID) tuple exists. The spec explicitly requires 'full unused (year,tmID) tuple' and 'program must re-verify post-generation'. No such composite-tuple verification exists.
issues.requested_revision: Implement composite-key unmatched-parent reservation: for each UNMATCHED_PARENT target that is part of a composite parent key, reserve a full parent tuple (all key components) never drawn together by any child row, and verify post-generation that at least one parent row with a non-NULL full key has no child. Do not treat composite-key components independently.

issues.evidence: spec.py GROUP_SIZE_TARGETS includes ('Master','playerID'), ('Master','firstName'), ('Goalies','playerID'). instance._plant_group_sizes picks three random non-NULL values and assigns them to six shuffled row indices to create groups of size 1, 2, 3. But for Master.playerID and Goalies.playerID these are FK-parent join keys; overwriting them with existing values can create duplicate parent keys that are then removed by the final sample_fresh_primary_keys re-dedup (Master.playerID is not a PK, but Goalies.playerID is part of the PK (playerID,year,stint)). For Goalies, planting group sizes on playerID then re-deduping by (playerID,year,stint) can drop rows and destroy the planted group structure. There is no post-dedup verification that groups of size 1, 2 and >=3 actually exist. The spec's uncertainty note explicitly says 'Group-size and duplicate planting must run after PK dedup and be followed by a re-dedup/assertion for composite PKs (Goalies, Scoring)' — the assertion is missing.
issues.requested_revision: After the final re-dedup, verify that the required group sizes (1, 2, >=3) exist for each GROUP_SIZE_TARGETS column; if not, re-plant on surviving rows (choosing rows whose PK components are not disturbed, or adjusting non-key columns) and re-verify. Add an explicit assertion.

issues.evidence: spec.py DUPLICATE_TARGETS includes ('Master','playerID'), ('Master','coachID'), ('Master','firstName'). instance._plant_duplicates overwrites 20-50% of rows with a single chosen value. For Master.playerID and Master.coachID these are FK-parent join keys; collapsing many rows to one value reduces the number of distinct parent values available to children, which can conflict with the unmatched-parent requirement (a non-NULL unused parent value must remain). The duplicate planting runs before _reserve_unmatched_parents, which may then have to rewrite child FKs, but there is no guarantee the duplicate share (20-50%) survives after _reserve_unmatched_parents rewrites child columns (it only rewrites children, not parents, so parent duplicates survive — but the interaction is not verified). More concretely, the spec requires '20-50% of rows share a value with another row' for DISTINCT-target columns; after _plant_duplicates the final sample_fresh_primary_keys/drop_unique_duplicates re-dedup runs, and for Master.playerID (not a PK, not unique) it survives, but for columns that are unique or PK the duplicates would be removed. Master.playerID/coachID/firstName are not unique/PK so this is acceptable, but no post-generation check confirms the 20-50% share.
issues.requested_revision: Add a post-generation verification that each DUPLICATE_TARGETS column has 20-50% of generated rows sharing a value with another row, and that this does not eliminate the non-NULL unused parent value required by UNMATCHED_PARENT. If the share is not met, re-plant on surviving rows.

issues.evidence: The spec's per_column_exceptions for Master.height comparison_boundary requires expression_values for CAST(REPLACE(master.height,'/','') AS INTEGER) with values [71,72,73] and plant_form 'at least one value of the form <tens>/<ones> (e.g. 7/1 -> 71)'. spec.py HEIGHT_SLASH_FORM = '7/1' and HeightSampler emits the slash form with 10% probability. However, the semantic rule is 'height IS NULL OR CAST(REPLACE(height,'/','') AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 60 AND 90'. The slash form '7/1' -> REPLACE -> '71' -> 71, which is in range. But HeightSampler.sample() only emits the slash form when the sampled integer has exactly two digits (len(s)==2); for a value like 100 (not possible here since hi=90) or single-digit it returns plain. This is fine. The real gap: the spec's BOUNDARY for ('Master','height') is ['71','72','73','74','75','76'] and the sampler's pool includes these, but the comparison_boundary target also lists values [71,72,73,74,75,76] as the boundary set for the predicate 'master.height > 72'. The program does not guarantee that at least one row has height exactly 72 and one exactly 73 (the equal-and-one-step-from boundary) — it only includes them in the pool with low probability. This is a minor coverage gap, not a hard-rule violation.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: clarify whether the height boundary requires guaranteed presence of the exact boundary values (72 and 73) or merely pool inclusion. If guaranteed presence is intended, add it to the spec as a planting target; otherwise document that pool inclusion suffices.

issues.evidence: The spec's generic_sampling_rules text_id says 'Sample from a pool of realistic identifier strings (lowercase letters + digits, 8-10 chars); 5% near-variants (case flip, one-char edit); 2% '' when nullable.' But the per_column_exceptions for Master.playerID comparison_boundary requires values ['', 'x', 'cleghsp01', 'CLEGHSP01', 'valiqst01', 'VALIQST01'] — these are 8-char lowercase+digits IDs plus case-flipped variants plus '' and 'x'. The IdSampler._fresh generates 8-10 char lowercase+digits, and _near_variant does case flip / trailing space / one-char edit. 'x' is a 1-char value not producible by _fresh (min 8 chars) and not a near-variant of an 8-char ID (one-char edit keeps length). So the boundary value 'x' for Master.playerID (and similarly 'x' for Master.coachID) is only reachable if 'x' happens to be in the literal pool or original values. The spec lists 'x' as a required boundary value but the program's IdSampler cannot generate it from its own pool unless seeded. This is a spec/program inconsistency for the boundary literal 'x'.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: either remove 'x' from the comparison_boundary values for Master.playerID/coachID (since it is not a realistic ID and not producible by the ID sampler), or add it explicitly to the boundary pool that the sampler draws from. Engineer: if kept, ensure BOUNDARY values are actually injected into the sampler pool (they are appended in _make_spec_sampler via _boundary_values, so 'x' would be in the pool — verify this path is exercised).

issues.evidence: The execution feedback shows rows_skipped for several tables: AwardsMisc 116, HOF 149, Teams 258, AwardsPlayers 346, Goalies 393, GoaliesSC 161, TeamSplits 27, TeamVsTeam 191, TeamsHalf 10, TeamsSC 12. These are rows that failed INSERT (PK/UNIQUE/NOT NULL/FK violations at write time). The writer counts them but the instance builder does not re-verify that the planted targets (group sizes, ties, duplicates, unmatched parents) survive after these skips. Since skipped rows are dropped at write time, any planted structure on a skipped row is lost. The spec requires post-generation verification of unmatched-parent and tie targets; the program's _reserve_unmatched_parents runs before writing, so it cannot account for write-time skips.
issues.requested_revision: Move target verification (unmatched-parent, group-size, tie, duplicate) to after the write step, or make the writer report which rows were skipped and re-verify targets on the actually-written rows. At minimum, document that write-time skips can invalidate planted targets and add a post-write verification pass.

issues.evidence: instance._apply_null_rule applies NULLs to every nullable column including FK child columns (e.g. Coaches.tmID, Goalies.tmID, Scoring.tmID, SeriesPost.tmIDWinner/Loser, TeamVsTeam.oppID). The execution feedback shows NULLs in these FK columns (e.g. 'Goalies.tmID: NULL 78 / 1671', 'Scoring.tmID: NULL 182 / 3609', 'SeriesPost.tmIDWinner: NULL 41 / 833'). The schema declares these columns nullable (no NOT NULL), so NULL FKs are allowed by SQLite. However, the spec's dependencies list these as child->parent FK relationships and the unmatched_join_rows targets require 'child_rows_with_null_fk: true' — so NULL child FKs are intended. This is consistent. But the spec's null_share rule says 'FK-parent join-key columns (Master.playerID, Master.coachID, Scoring.playerID) get at most 20% NULL' — it does not mention other FK child columns. The program applies the compact null share (5-30%) to all nullable FK child columns, which is consistent with the general null_share rule. No issue here, but note that the spec's FK_PARENT_NULL_CAP is only applied to UNMATCHED_PARENT entries, not to all FK columns; this is a minor documentation gap.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: clarify whether the 20% NULL cap applies only to FK-parent join-key columns listed in UNMATCHED_PARENT or to all FK columns. Engineer: if the cap is meant to be broader, apply it consistently.

unresolved_checks: Whether the planted aggregate ties (SUM(SHO), COALESCE(SHO,0), COUNT(*) by birthCountry) actually survive the final PK/UNIQUE re-dedup and write-time skips — no post-generation assertion exists.
Whether a full unused (year,tmID) tuple exists for the Teams composite-key unmatched-parent target — the program treats components independently.
Whether group sizes 1, 2, >=3 survive for Goalies.playerID after composite-PK re-dedup — no assertion.
Whether the 20-50% duplicate share is achieved for Master.playerID/coachID/firstName after all planting and dedup — no assertion.
Whether the boundary literal 'x' for Master.playerID/coachID is actually reachable given the IdSampler's 8-10 char minimum — depends on pool seeding.
Whether write-time skipped rows (e.g. 393 Goalies rows) invalidate any planted target — not verified post-write.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows verify_errors on nearly every instance for targets the spec explicitly requires: duplicate:Master.playerID (20/20), duplicate:Master.coachID (20/20), duplicate:Master.firstName (20/20), tie:sum:Goalies.playerID (20/20), tie:count:Master.birthCountry (19/20), unmatched:Teams.year (20/20), unmatched:Teams.tmID (20/20), unmatched_composite:Teams (4/20), unmatched:Master.playerID (2/20), unmatched:Coaches.coachID (5/20), group_size:Goalies.playerID (1/20). The program's own verify_targets() reports these as failures, so the planted structure did not survive on the written rows.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the planting/verification pipeline so the spec's targets actually hold on written rows. Concretely: (a) _plant_duplicates sets a single value v on k rows, but for Master.playerID/coachID the subsequent sample_fresh_primary_keys re-dedups on the PK (playerID is the PK of Master), so duplicates are removed — duplicates_for_distinct on a PK column is contradictory and must be reconciled (either the spec must not list PK columns as duplicate targets, or the program must not re-dedup them); (b) _plant_ties for SUM(SHO) sets SHO='5' on two rows but does not guarantee those two rows belong to two distinct players with no other player exceeding 5 after the re-dedup and write-time skips — the tie is lost; (c) _reserve_unmatched_parents/_reserve_unmatched_composite run before write-time skips and are not re-applied, so Teams.year/tmID unmatched targets fail on 20/20 instances; (d) group_size:Goalies.playerID fails on 1 instance. Re-verify after write and, if a target is lost, repair or regenerate rather than silently reporting a verify_error.

issues.evidence: The spec lists Master.playerID and Master.coachID under both duplicates_for_distinct (20-50% duplicate share) and as primary/join keys. Master.playerID is the primary key of Master (schema: playerID TEXT, and it is the FK target of AwardsPlayers/Scoring/etc.), and Master.coachID is a FK to Coaches.coachID. Requiring 20-50% duplicate share on a PK column is unsatisfiable together with the fresh_pk rule 'unique per instance' and the program's re-dedup. The execution feedback confirms this: duplicate:Master.playerID and duplicate:Master.coachID fail on 20/20 instances.
issues.requested_revision: Remove Master.playerID and Master.coachID from DUPLICATE_TARGETS (or restrict duplicates_for_distinct to non-key columns), since the schema makes them unique/join keys. Keep duplicate targets only on genuinely non-key columns (e.g. Master.firstName).

issues.evidence: The spec's NULL rule (interface rule 7) requires that for every nullable column each instance contains generated rows with NULL and rows with non-NULL values, with a NULL share following the compact database's share. The execution feedback shows many nullable columns with NULL 0 / n or with NULL shares far from the compact share, e.g. AwardsMisc.award NULL 10/167, AwardsMisc.lgID NULL 10/167, HOF.category NULL 8/216, HOF.name NULL 12/216, HOF.year NULL 13/216, Teams.name NULL 33/662, Teams.rank NULL 33/662, Teams.G NULL 34/662, Scoring.playerID NULL 621/3609 (17%), Master.playerID NULL 472/3876 (12%). More importantly, _apply_null_rule applies a uniform 5-30% share to every nullable column regardless of the compact share, and for NOT NULL columns it skips — but the feedback shows NULLs on columns that are NOT NULL in the schema (e.g. AwardsMisc.award is nullable in schema, but HOF.category is nullable in schema too; however Teams.name is nullable). The real problem is that the NULL share is not derived from the compact database share as the spec requires ('following the compact database's share for that column'), and several columns get 0 NULLs.
issues.requested_revision: Make _apply_null_rule use the compact share per column (it already computes _compact_null_share but then clamps to [0.05,0.30] and overrides with max(1,...)), and ensure at least one NULL and at least one non-NULL per nullable column. For columns where the compact share is 0, the spec's 'following the compact database's share' would give 0 NULLs, which conflicts with 'at least one NULL row per nullable column' — the designer should clarify which takes precedence, and the engineer should implement the chosen rule consistently.

issues.evidence: The spec's hard_bounds rule says 'All range, enum and order rules in semantic_rules_and_formulas are hard constraints: every generated row must satisfy them on non-NULL operands; clamp numeric output to [lo,hi] after any jitter.' The program's NumberSampler clamps to [min,max], but the enum samplers (EnumSampler, NameSampler, IdSampler) apply _near_variant which can produce values outside the enum (e.g. case-flipped 'nhl' for lgID, 'Toronto ' with trailing space for birthCountry). The spec's semantic rules require lgID IN ('NHL','WHA',...) and confID IN ('CC','WA','WC','EC') etc. on non-NULL operands. The execution feedback does not show enum violations directly, but the near-variant logic in EnumSampler.sample() (u < 0.05 -> _near_variant) can emit 'nhl' or 'Nhl' which violates the enum rule. Similarly NameSampler for birthCountry can emit 'toronto' or 'Toronto ' which violates the comparison-boundary intent but not a hard enum (birthCountry has no enum rule), yet for lgID/confID/divID it does violate.
issues.requested_revision: Do not apply _near_variant to columns governed by a hard enum rule (lgID, confID, divID, HOF.category, AwardsCoaches.award, AwardsPlayers.pos, AwardsMisc.award, AwardsMisc.lgID, CombinedShutouts.R/P, Master.shootCatch, abbrev.Type, Teams.playoff, SeriesPost.round). Either drop near-variants for these columns or restrict near-variants to columns without enum constraints. The spec's comparison_boundary values (e.g. 'usa','toronto') are for columns without enum rules (birthCountry, coachID) and should be injected verbatim, not via near-variant.

issues.evidence: The spec's per_column_exceptions for Master.height requires 'at least one value of the form <tens>/<ones> (e.g. 7/1 -> 71) so the REPLACE expression is exercised' and 'at least one row with height exactly 72 and one with 73'. The program's _enforce_height_boundary sets h[idx[0]]='72' and h[idx[1]]='73' (plain form), and HeightSampler emits slash form with 10% probability. However, _enforce_height_boundary runs before sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates, and Master has no PK on height, so the 72/73 rows survive — but the slash form is only probabilistic (10%), not guaranteed. The spec says 'plant_form: at least one value of the form <tens>/<ones>', which is a guarantee, not a probability.
issues.requested_revision: Guarantee at least one slash-form height (e.g. set one row to '7/1' explicitly in _enforce_height_boundary, in addition to the exact '72' and '73'), so the REPLACE expression is deterministically exercised.

issues.evidence: The spec's ties rule says 'when the tie target is an aggregate (SUM/COUNT/COALESCE), construct the underlying per-group values so the aggregate ties at the specified rank with no smaller value present, and plant after PK/UNIQUE dedup and NULL application; re-verify after final re-dedup and after write-time skips.' The program's _plant_ties for kind='sum' sets SHO='5' on two rows but does not ensure those two rows are for two distinct players (it picks vals[0], vals[1] from the playerID column, which may be the same player after dedup), and it caps other SHO values at 5 but does not ensure no other player's SUM exceeds 5 (a player with two rows of SHO=3 has SUM=6 > 5). The execution feedback shows tie:sum:Goalies.playerID fails on 20/20 instances.
issues.requested_revision: For the SUM(SHO) tie, pick two distinct playerIDs, set each to a single Goalies row with SHO=5, and set every other player's per-player SUM(SHO) strictly below 5 (e.g. cap each other player's total SHO at 4). Re-verify after write-time skips and repair if the tie is lost.

issues.evidence: The spec's ties rule for COUNT(*) by birthCountry requires 'two birthCountry values with equal counts' at rank 1. The program's _plant_ties for kind='count' sets k = max(1, n//8) rows to v1 and k rows to v2, but does not ensure no other birthCountry value has a higher count (the original sampler may already have produced a value with more than k occurrences). The execution feedback shows tie:count:Master.birthCountry fails on 19/20 instances.
issues.requested_revision: For the COUNT(*) tie, after planting v1 and v2 with equal counts, verify that no other birthCountry value has a count greater than the planted count; if so, reduce the other counts (reassign rows) or increase the planted counts. Re-verify after write-time skips.

issues.evidence: The spec's unmatched_parent rule requires 'reserve at least one non-NULL parent value (or full parent tuple for composite keys) never drawn by any child; verify after generation and after write-time skips that at least one parent row with a non-NULL key has no child.' The program's _reserve_unmatched_parents and _reserve_unmatched_composite run before write-time skips and are not re-applied after skips. The execution feedback shows unmatched:Teams.year (20/20), unmatched:Teams.tmID (20/20), unmatched_composite:Teams (4/20), unmatched:Master.playerID (2/20), unmatched:Coaches.coachID (5/20) all fail.
issues.requested_revision: Re-run the unmatched-parent reservation after write-time skips (or verify on kept rows and repair by rewriting a child FK to a different parent value). For composite keys (Teams.(year,tmID)), ensure the full tuple is reserved and re-verified on kept rows.

issues.evidence: The spec's per_column_exceptions for Master.playerID lists comparison_boundary values ['', 'x', 'cleghsp01', 'CLEGHSP01', 'valiqst01', 'VALIQST01'] and notes "'x' injected into sampler pool verbatim". However, Master.playerID is the primary key of Master and the FK target of AwardsPlayers/Scoring/etc. Injecting '' and 'x' as playerID values creates parent rows with degenerate keys, and the spec's own unmatched_join_rows target requires 'non-NULL unused parent value only' — '' is non-NULL but degenerate. The spec does not clarify whether '' counts as a valid non-NULL parent value for the unmatched target. The execution feedback shows unmatched:Master.playerID fails on 2/20 instances.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify whether '' is a valid non-NULL parent value for the unmatched-parent target. If not, exclude '' from the boundary pool for Master.playerID (and Master.coachID) or document that the unmatched target must be satisfied by a non-empty non-NULL value. Also clarify whether 'x' (a 1-char ID) is acceptable as a PK value given the schema's TEXT type.

issues.evidence: The spec's generic_sampling_rules text_id says 'Sample from a pool of realistic identifier strings (lowercase letters + digits, 8-10 chars); 5% near-variants (case flip, one-char edit); 2% '' when nullable; boundary literals from per_column_exceptions are injected into the pool verbatim.' The program's IdSampler._fresh emits 8-10 chars, but the boundary literals 'x', 'cleghsp01', 'CLEGHSP01', 'valiqst01', 'VALIQST01' are injected into the pool via _make_spec_sampler (pool += [str(v) for v in _boundary_values(table, name)]). However, IdSampler.sample() applies _near_variant with 5% probability, which can turn 'cleghsp01' into 'CLEGHSP01' or 'cleghsp01 ' — this is fine for the boundary target (both forms are in the pool), but the 2% '' when nullable is applied on top of the boundary pool, so '' may be emitted even when the boundary target wants a non-empty value. The spec's comparison_boundary for Master.playerID includes '' as a target value, so this is consistent, but the interaction with unmatched_join_rows (which needs a non-NULL unused parent) is not guaranteed.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure that when a boundary literal is injected, it is emitted verbatim at least once (not only via the 5% near-variant path), and that the '' boundary value does not consume the only unused non-NULL parent value needed for the unmatched target. Add a post-generation check that each boundary literal appears at least once in the written rows.

issues.evidence: The spec's semantic_rules_and_formulas includes Master.deathYear >= birthYear when both non-NULL, enforced by resampling. The program's _enforce_death_after_birth resamples deathYear to rng.randint(bi, spec.YEAR_MAX) when di < bi. However, this runs before sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates, and Master has no PK on deathYear, so the resampled values survive. But the resampling uses spec.YEAR_MAX=2011, which may produce deathYear > 2011 if birthYear is close to 2011 — actually randint(bi, 2011) is bounded by 2011, so this is fine. The execution feedback does not show a violation, so this appears implemented correctly. No issue.
issues.requested_revision: No change needed; noted as verified.

issues.evidence: The spec's table_sizes_per_instance gives exact sizes (e.g. Teams: 40, Master: 200), but the program's choose_table_sizes jitters each size by 0.5 + rng.random() and clamps to [0,230]. The execution feedback shows rows_added far exceeding the spec sizes (e.g. Master 3876 vs spec 200, Scoring 3609 vs spec 200, TeamVsTeam 3941 vs spec 200). This is because the program appends generated rows on top of the compact database (which already has rows), and the spec's table_sizes_per_instance is interpreted as the number of generated rows, not total rows. The spec does not explicitly say whether table_sizes_per_instance is the number of generated rows or total rows. The execution feedback's rows_added suggests the program generates ~10-20x the spec size, which may be intentional (jitter) but the magnitude is large.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the spec whether table_sizes_per_instance is the number of generated rows or total rows, and whether jitter is allowed. If jitter is allowed, document the range (the program uses 0.5-1.5x). The current 10-20x discrepancy between spec size and rows_added suggests either the spec size is a minimum or the program is over-generating; align the two.

unresolved_checks: Whether '' is a valid non-NULL parent value for the unmatched-parent target (designer clarification needed).
Whether table_sizes_per_instance is generated rows or total rows, and whether jitter is allowed (designer clarification needed).
Whether the compact database's NULL share should override the 'at least one NULL per nullable column' rule when the compact share is 0 (designer clarification needed).

Whether near-variants are allowed on enum-constrained columns (the spec's hard_bounds rule says enums are hard constraints, but the generic_sampling_rules text_id/text_short say 5% near-variants; these conflict for enum columns).
